newsitem.title: ITALY: Ex-SS captain says some Italians want him dead.
newsitem.headline: Ex-SS captain says some Italians want him dead.

text.p: Former SS captain Erich Priebke, being held in jail in Rome after a war crimes trial, said in an interview published on Monday he believed some people in Italy would like to see him dead.

Priebke, 83, was tried earlier this year by an Italian military court. The trial ended on August 1 with a verdict finding him guilty but ordering him freed because the statute of limitations for his crimes had run out.

The German, who had lived openly for almost 50 years in Argentina, was blocked inside the courthouse by protesters angry with the verdict. He was re-arrested hours later when Germany said it intended to extradite him for a war crimes trial there.

"To know you are a free man and then to be immediately defrauded of this liberty left me very depressed," Priebke told the newspaper Il Giornale in an interview from Rome's Regina Coeli jail. "Nevertheless I'm holding up."
Priebke was tried for his role in the SS massacre of 335 Italian men and boys in March 1944 in the Ardeatine Caves south of Rome, the worst atrocity committed in Italy in World War Two.
Seventy-five of the victims were Jews. The SS ordered the massacre in retaliation for a bomb attack by partisans in Rome which killed 33 German soldiers.
Priebke admitted shooting two people and checking off names from a list at the caves, but his lawyers argued he should not be held responsible because he had to follow orders or be killed himself.
Priebke remains in jail while various legal motions relating to his future work their way through the Italian court system.

On Tuesday, Italy's Supreme Court will consider a request by the prosecution and civil plaintiffs that the verdict be overturned because they believe the lead trial judge, Agostino Quistelli, was biased in Priebke's favour. If the request is granted, they would seek a new Priebke trial in Italy.
Germany's extradition request also is pending.

"Having read (Quistelli's) sentence -- which despite clearing me, in substance found me guilty -- I am amazed that they still want his recusal," Priebke said. "They want me to spend my life in jail, they want me dead."

Priebke said he did not understand Germany's extradition request because he had never tried to conceal his identity while living in the Andean ski resort of Bariloche, where he ran a hotel and was active in community affairs.
"I shook hands with various German ambassadors and I received more than one delegation of the German parliament, and many visitors from Germany," he said.
"After the war I was in Germany at least 10 times and always as Erich Priebke," he said. "I visited Italy twice with my wife. Never, not in Germany nor in Italy, did they ever accuse me of anything."
Priebke was arrested and susequently extradited to Italy last November after he admitted his role in the Ardeatine Caves massacre to a U.S. television crew in 1994.
